title: Filtration: separating sand from water
examples: How do you separate sand and water?
Can you filter salt out of water?

explain.say: Imagine you dropped a handful of sand into your glass of water. Oops! How could you get clean water back? Look at the board. We start with this muddy mixture of sand and water.

stages.label: Filter paper cone
stages.note: A paper cone sits in a funnel.

stages.label: Residue stays
stages.note: Sand is caught in the paper.

explain.say: See the second step? You fold a circle of filter paper into a cone and put it in a funnel. The paper is full of tiny holes, far too small to see. What do you think can fit through them?

stages.label: Filter paper cone
stages.note: A paper cone sits in a funnel.

stages.label: Residue stays
stages.note: Sand is caught in the paper.

explain.say: Right, only the water! Pour the mixture in slowly. Water particles are tiny, so they slip through the holes. Look at the drops on the board. Sand grains are far too big. Can you spot the same idea in your tea strainer?

stages.label: Filter paper cone
stages.note: A paper cone sits in a funnel.

stages.label: Residue stays
stages.note: Sand is caught in the paper.

explain.say: Look at the last step. The clear water that drips through is the filtrate. The sand left in the paper is the residue, which means what remains. Can you say which one is the clean water?

explain.say: Brilliant! But filtering only removes things that do not dissolve. Dissolved salt slips straight through the paper with the water. Wow: coffee machines, car engines and even your kidneys filter things every single day.

faq.a: Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid, like sand from water or tea leaves from tea. Insoluble means it does not dissolve.
Filter paper has tiny holes. Liquid particles and dissolved particles are small enough to pass through, but bigger solid grains get stuck.
asks: Why does water go through filter paper?

faq.a: The residue is the solid left behind in the filter paper, like the sand.
asks: What is left in the filter paper?

faq.a: The filtrate is the liquid that passes through the filter paper and collects below.

faq.q: Can you filter salt out of salt water?
faq.a: No. Salt is dissolved, and its particles are tiny, so they pass through the paper with the water. You need evaporation instead.

facts: Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid; the solid left behind is the residue and the liquid that passes through is the filtrate.
Dissolved substances pass through filter paper, so filtration cannot separate a solution.
